Get started with FunMel

Source: vignettes/FunMel.Rmd
FunMel.Rmd

START WITH REAL PHOTOGRAPHS

Prepare. Measure. Inspect. Compare.

Run eight original plate photographs through the complete workflow, using supplied treatment/control assignments and the final matched-control figure.

01 · Run this example

Follow the five steps below. The photographs and metadata are included.

02 · Understand the results

The detailed real-data tutorial explains QC, measurements, statistics and exports.

03 · Use your photographs

Follow the own-ZIP workflow with your experimental assignments.

1. Install and load

Install once. After an update, restart R before loading FunMel. In RStudio, choose Session → Restart R.

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mghotbi/FunMel")
library(FunMel)

Source installation requires Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS, matching Rtools on Windows, or R development tools and ImageMagick development libraries on Linux. R >= 4.1 is required. To install the tutorials for offline use, add build_vignettes=TRUE to install_github().

2. Prepare the real-data example

Run these steps in order. The eight photographs contain two sets, each with three fungal confrontation plates and one control plate. The supplied metadata already identifies each plate’s treatment, own control and segmentation layout; no metadata entry or approval-flag edits are needed for this example.

photos <- system.file("extdata", "14-days", package="FunMel")
project_dir <- tempfile("FunMel_real_example_")
project <- prepare_experiment(input=photos, project_dir=project_dir)
project$project_dir
#> [1] "/private/var/folders/f1/f8pqw4_n4y90tlykbbhy3ztm0000gn/T/RtmpUBOROy/FunMel_real_example_1b88708d0af3"

tempfile() supplies a new temporary folder name, so repeating the example creates a separate project without overwriting earlier work. Keep the printed folder location: all outputs will be saved there. To retain this practice run, copy the complete project folder to a permanent location before closing R.

3. Measure and inspect

The 90-mm diameter below is an illustrative calibration. Verify the actual outer dish diameter before using measurements scientifically. The workflow measures the four target colonies on each plate and requests five circular spots per colony.

result <- run_experiment(
  project, dish_diameter_mm=90, max_dim=1200,
  n_spots=5, spot_radius_mm=0.4, n_boot=20
)
result$analysis_status
#> [1] "complete"
result$failed
#> [1] file  error
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
project$qc_dir
#> [1] "/private/var/folders/f1/f8pqw4_n4y90tlykbbhy3ztm0000gn/T/RtmpUBOROy/FunMel_real_example_1b88708d0af3/qc"

The expected status is "complete" with zero failed photographs. Open the printed QC folder and inspect the target-colony masks, central fungal tissue and hyphae, sampling spots, scale and lighting before interpreting results. QC reminders do not require changing approval flags. Resolve genuine failed photographs before finalizing. The 20 bootstrap resamples keep this practice run quick; they are not intended for precise uncertainty estimates.

Inspect the measurements directly:

knitr::kable(head(result$colonies[c("plate_id", "colony_id", "MI_mean")]),
             digits=3, row.names=FALSE)
plate_id colony_id MI_mean

2026_10_02_99_38 TR 72.105
2026_10_02_99_38 BR 74.293
2026_10_02_99_38 BL 69.635
2026_10_02_99_39 TL 71.186
2026_10_02_99_39 TR 68.283

             digits=3, row.names=FALSE)
plate_id colony_id spot_id MI_mean

4. Calculate coefficients and display the final figure

Finalization reuses the saved measurements and matches each treatment to its own set’s control.

reviewed <- finish_experiment(project)
knitr::kable(reviewed$melanization_coefficient[
  c("set_id", "treatment", "MI_treatment_mean", "MI_control_mean",
    "melanization_coefficient", "n_treatment_plates", "n_control_plates")],
  digits=3, row.names=FALSE)
set_id treatment MI_treatment_mean MI_control_mean melanization_coefficient n_treatment_plates n_control_plates
A60_2_14_days A60_2 68.996 42.374 1.628 3 1
B20_2_14_days B20_2 67.463 51.813 1.302 3 1 
comparison <- plot_treatment_comparison(reviewed)
if (!is.null(comparison)) print(comparison)

The left panel shows plate melanization indices; the right panel shows matched-control coefficients. Squares are controls, circles are treatment plates and lower diamonds are treatment means. Bars show one between-plate SD, not confidence intervals. Each set has only one control, so control SD and replicated-control significance tests are unavailable.

MI is 100 - CIELAB L*, an image-darkness proxy rather than a direct measurement of melanin concentration. Colonies and spots within a plate are subsamples; independent plates are the experimental units. See the detailed real-data tutorial for interpretation and limitations.

5. Find outputs and reopen saved work 

project$project_dir
#> [1] "/private/var/folders/f1/f8pqw4_n4y90tlykbbhy3ztm0000gn/T/RtmpUBOROy/FunMel_real_example_1b88708d0af3"

This folder contains colony, spot, profile and plate CSV tables; matched coefficients; saved R analyses; QC images; and the final treatment_comparison.pdf, .svg and .png. Statistics and the explanatory caption are saved separately. The exported figure has no embedded caption by default.

After saving or moving the complete project folder, reopen it without preparing or measuring again:

project <- load_experiment() # Select project.rds in the saved project folder.
result <- read_experiment(project)
reviewed <- read_experiment(project, finalized=TRUE)
print(plot_treatment_comparison(reviewed))

Use your own photographs

Follow the own-ZIP workflow for separate input/output paths, preparation, reopening and measurement. Your photographs may have any supported names and any actual treatment codes; the bundled assignments apply only to the supplied photographs.

Measurements do not require treatment names or approval flags. A mixed collection still needs correct per-image layouts: fungus for confrontations and none for controls. Matched coefficients need real treatment/control assignments within set_id; otherwise measurements are saved with awaiting_design. For exploration without treatment names, use the set-only measurement plot. Every custom metadata column is retained.

For specialist calibration, classification and measurement utilities, see the complete function examples.
